title: Games
subtitle: Design and ship your own game with Claude: learn what makes games fun, remix a classic game type with your own twist, then plan, build, art up, level, balance and launch an original game, with a leaderboard and a Claude-powered character.
bigIdea: Every game has a goal, rules, a challenge and feedback, wrapped around a small core loop you repeat. Fun comes from challenge that's just right, and from feedback that feels great. Claude can write the code, but you are the game designer: you find the fun, tune the numbers, watch real players, and make it fair, kind and your own.
objectives: Explain what makes a game fun: goal, rules, challenge, feedback and the core loop.
Build small games with Claude and tune them by changing numbers and adding mechanics.
Remix a classic game type into an original game with a twist, using no copied names, characters or art.
Plan an original game on one page and build it with Claude Code, deployed on Vercel.
Add original art and sound, levels with a difficulty curve, and balance it with playtest numbers.
Add a fair leaderboard and a safe Claude-powered feature, then playtest, polish and launch a game that's accessible, fair and kind.

vocabulary.definition: The small set of actions you repeat again and again in a game.
One thing the player can do.
What a game repeats many times a second: check input, update, draw.
vocabulary.analogy: A flip book that flips itself 60 times a second.
vocabulary.example: Read keys → move the cat → draw the screen.

vocabulary.definition: When two things in a game touch.
vocabulary.example: The basket touches a falling star: +1 point.

vocabulary.definition: A kind of game with familiar mechanics.
vocabulary.analogy: A recipe type, like 'soup', with many versions.
vocabulary.example: Endless runner, maze chase, grid puzzle.

vocabulary.definition: Making something new from a familiar idea, with your own twist, name and art.
vocabulary.analogy: A new song using a classic beat.
vocabulary.example: Paddle-and-ball, but you're a whale bouncing a bubble.

vocabulary.definition: Extra feedback that makes actions feel great: sounds, sparkles, a tiny shake.
vocabulary.example: A 'ding!' and sparkles when you collect a coin.

vocabulary.definition: One page that says what your game is and how it works.
vocabulary.analogy: A recipe card for your game.
vocabulary.example: Pitch, player, core loop, mechanics, win/lose, controls, look, scope.

vocabulary.definition: How big a project is. Keep it small enough to finish.
vocabulary.analogy: Choosing a pizza you can actually eat.
vocabulary.example: 1 level type, 3 difficulty steps, no story mode.

vocabulary.definition: A picture of one thing in the game.
vocabulary.analogy: A sticker you move around a page.
vocabulary.example: The player, a coin, a bug.

vocabulary.definition: How a game gets harder over time.
vocabulary.analogy: Training wheels coming off, bit by bit.
vocabulary.example: Level 1 teaches, level 2 practices, level 3 tests.

vocabulary.definition: When the challenge matches your skill, so it's fun, not boring or stressful.
vocabulary.analogy: A talk with a friend that's not too easy and not too hard.
vocabulary.example: You lose sometimes, but always want one more try.

vocabulary.definition: Making a game fair and fun: no part too easy, too hard or too random.
vocabulary.analogy: Making sure both teams have a fair chance.
vocabulary.example: Making a power-up last 5 seconds instead of 30.

vocabulary.definition: A ranked list of the best scores from many players.
A non-player character: someone in the game the computer controls.
vocabulary.analogy: An actor in a play who isn't you.
vocabulary.example: A gardener who gives tips between levels.

vocabulary.definition: Watching people play your game to see what works.
vocabulary.analogy: A taste test before a bake sale.
vocabulary.example: 3 new players, you watch silently and take notes.

gamification.questLine: The Guild's arcade: remix a classic game type with your own twist, then design and ship your own original game.
gamification.badge: 🕹️ Game Designer: an original, launched game that scores 3 or more on every rubric row.
gamification.boss: Game Launch Arcade: a 3-minute trailer-style pitch, then guests play your game on their own devices and fill the leaderboard. 1-on-1: launch for the teacher plus 2 or 3 guests.
sideQuests: Daily challenge: a level that's the same for everyone each day, with its own leaderboard (+25 XP).
Sprite sheet: give your main character a walking motion (+25 XP).
Read the code: explain your game loop's code line by line in plain words (+25 XP).
Level editor: let players make and share their own level (+25 XP).

safety.teach: Game types and mechanics are free to use; specific games' names, characters, art, music and levels are not. Make your own, and keep a Credits screen for every sound or picture you didn't make.
Gentle flashes and shakes with an 'effects off' option, mute, pause, easy mode, color plus shapes or icons, keyboard and touch controls.
Nicknames only, a rude-word filter, score limits and Row Level Security. Only test cheating on your own games or with permission.
Key only on the server, daily limits, fallback lines, short answers, stay in character, kind and age-appropriate, no personal questions.
No guilt timers, streak punishments, pay-to-win or loot boxes. Design for people being glad they played, not for pressure.

finalProject.title: Remix a Classic Game Type, Then Ship Your Own Game
finalProject.brief: First, remix a classic game type (paddle-and-ball, brick breaker, grid puzzle, endless runner, maze chase or snake-style) into an original game with your own name, art and twist, and show it at the Remix Arcade. Then plan, build and launch your own original game with Claude Code: levels, balance, art and sound, a fair leaderboard and an optional Claude-powered character, tested with real players. In a group, launch to the class. 1-on-1, launch to the teacher and guests.
deliverables: Remix: an original take on a classic game type with a twist and game juice (published artifact link)
One-Page Game Plan and a gray-box prototype
Live game on Vercel with its GitHub repo, playable on phone and computer
Original art and sound with a Credits screen
3+ levels or waves, a settings table and playtest numbers showing a balance change
High score and a fair leaderboard; optional AI character with limits and fallbacks
Playtest notes, sorted bug list, Fair & Fun Checklist and patch notes

levels: No clear goal or core loop
A core loop, but it's not fun yet or the scope is too big
Clear goal, fun core loop, levels that teach → practice → test
Design choices explained with game words, and a twist that makes it feel fresh
Runs, but missing screens or feels flat
All game states work, original art and sound, juice that fits, live on phone and computer
Polished, responsive and juicy; bugs triaged and fixed; student explains the game loop
Settings table, playtest numbers and a measured balance change; 3+ playtesters
Several data-driven changes with before-and-after numbers; players say 'one more try!'
Copied characters or art, or unfair design
Mostly original, some checklist items missing
Original with credits, Fair & Fun Checklist passes, safe leaderboard and AI
Welcoming to many kinds of players, with access options, and explains how it avoids pressure tricks

finalProject.levelUp: Add a daily challenge or a level editor, and get 5 players outside class onto your leaderboard.

support: Ready-made prompts for each build step, with blanks to fill.
Start the remix with the simplest types (paddle-and-ball or snake-style).
A smaller own game (one level type with 3 waves, local high score, no AI character) can still reach level 3 on most rows.
Group: Designer and Tester roles, swapping each lesson. 1-on-1: the student designs and builds, you playtest out loud.
extension: A boss level or a level editor.
Server-checked scores with a Vercel function.
Claude-generated riddles or level names, checked by code before showing.
Controls players can change, and subtitles.

carryForward: The game, and every project from the year, comes together at Demo Day (Module 7).
